frames.narration: A new instance of the orders service starts. It registers with the registry in its own zone: name, address, port, zone, version, weight. Its state is 'starting', so no one calls it yet.

The health checker calls the instance's health endpoint, which checks its database connection. It answers yes, so the instance becomes 'up' and gets a lease of 30 seconds. It will send a heartbeat every 10 seconds.
The registry gives the change a version number and pushes a small event down the watch stream. It also replicates the change to the registry in zone B, without waiting for an answer.

The checkout service has a local cache of the orders instances. It applies event 4,811 after 4,810, so it knows it missed nothing, and it starts to choose among 20 instances. No call ever went to the registry.

Later orders-7 is killed by the kernel and says nothing. The heartbeats stop. The lease of 30 seconds is the registry's only way to know, so for up to 30 seconds callers may still pick it, and the first failed connection is retried on another instance.

The lease runs out and the sweep removes the instance, and the event reaches every watcher. Meanwhile, if a switch had cut off 8 of 20 instances, only 12 of 20 would renew, which is 60 percent and below the 85 percent threshold, so the registry would stop expiring anything and keep the last list.
A planned shutdown goes better. The instance marks itself draining, deregisters, waits 5 seconds for the caches to catch up, finishes its current requests, and exits. Callers see no errors at all.
